title: Puncturing any coordinates of a full root tower preserves a supplied lisse module
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ use all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart, and $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ a reduced strict normal crossings boundary whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale and put
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\leq d\leq r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right).$$
The index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility, with transition $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. Let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a profinite set $P$ let $T[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_a}\coprod_{P_a}T$, and let $\mathcal N_P$ be the pullback of $\mathcal N$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects].
For $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ let $T_A^\circ=T\times_U U[1/\prod_{a\in A}t_a]$ and $j_{A,P}:T_A^\circ[P]\hookrightarrow T[P]$. The actual derived open-adjunction unit is an isomorphism
$$\mathcal N_P[0]\longrightarrow R(j_{A,P})_*j_{A,P}^*\mathcal N_P[0].$$
For $A=\varnothing$ it is the identity. These units and their inverses are natural in $P$, in maps of the supplied lisse modules, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. They commute with automorphisms preserving the indicated opens and with their actions on the supplied modules. For a profinite family of such automorphisms indexed by $Q$, compatibility means equality on the $Q$-parametrized terms themselves. Rank zero and the empty chart are included.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] and [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], pullback for the fixed condensed ring $C_F$ is exact and is the inverse image with transported scalar action. In particular it carries $C_{F,X}$ to $C_{F,X'}$, hence finite free modules to finite free modules (used in step 2), and it respects composition. Thus use the actual derived adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] throughout, also for $F=\Omega$; no finite-subextension replacement is made.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-tower-profinite-base-change] with $R_P=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}LC(P,\mathbf Z)$. It identifies $T[P]$ and $T_A^\circ[P]$ with the full tower and its indicated principal open over the affine pro-etale chart $U[P]$. The pulled-back finite-free trivializations of [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] make $\mathcal N_P$ lisse. These identifications also hold after any affine pro-etale chart base change.

proof.text: On this tower put $X_J=T[P][1/\prod_{b\in J}t_b]$ and $K_J=\mathcal N_P|_{X_J}[0]$. For every $a\notin J$, [lem-sfb-root-coordinate-supported-vanishing] gives $R\underline\Gamma_{V(t_a)}K_J=0$: its original chart hypotheses persist because $U[P]\to B$ is affine pro-etale. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-principal-support-unit-assembly]. Its conclusion is invertibility of the specified unit for $j_{A,P}$, independently of any ordering of $A$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-clean-open-unit-parametrized-exchange] to a parameter map or a pro-etale chart change: step 2 identifies the pullback tower and step 3 supplies both invertible units. Its equations prove compatibility with the canonical exchange and with maps of the supplied modules, including the inverses. For an action family $a:T[P][Q]\to T[P]$, use its supplied action isomorphism with the projection pullback. Step 3 gives the projection unit; the same lemma gives the action equation on the entire parameter scheme. By [lem-sfb-root-tower-profinite-base-change] that scheme is $T[P\times Q]$. Taking $Q=*$ gives individual automorphisms.

proof.text: For $A=\varnothing$ the open is the identity and so is its normalized unit; this includes $r=0$. At rank zero all terms are zero. An empty parameter or chart gives the empty scheme and the zero module category. The displayed equations remain identities in these cases.
